title: The market inspector comes
body: The muhtasib, the officer who watches over the markets, is walking down your street. Bishr found a few sacks of dates in the warehouse that have gone bad. He asks what to do.

choices.label: Throw the sacks out now
choices.hint: It costs money. The inspector will see an honest house.

choices.label: Hide the sacks and hope
choices.hint: It costs 4 in two seasons. Bad food is easy to smell, but your street hears nothing yet.

note: In 1341 the muhtasib of Cairo found 1,196 pigeons and 33,000 starlings, all spoiled, in a seller's storehouse. The man was punished in public, and the birds were destroyed.

title: A rich man wants a title
body: Tamer is a rich merchant. He hopes the sultan will name him chief of the merchants, a title given to some wealthy men. He asks your house to speak well of him at court. His rivals ask you to stay out.

choices.label: Speak well of Tamer at court
choices.hint: He will not forget it. His rivals will not either.

choices.label: Stay out of it
choices.hint: No one is angry, and no one owes you.

note: Sultans gave the title "chief of the merchants" to some rich men. One scholar warns that it was not a real office.

sources.at: pp. 150, 152 and 154; the title ra'is al-tujjar and Ashtor's warning

title: The elders hear a loss
body: Daud is a friend of yours. He gave Isaac 70 dinars to trade overseas, and Isaac lost almost 50 of them. Isaac says the loss is bad luck, and that Daud has no claim on him. Daud asks your house to help. You can ask the elders of your community to hear it, or take it to a judge.

choices.label: Ask the elders to hear it
choices.hint: They may tell you to let it go.

choices.label: Press Daud's claim before a judge
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now and pays back 9 in two seasons. Daud will thank you in coin. Isaac will not forgive it.

note: In one Geniza case an investor lost almost 50 of 70 dinars given to a trader going overseas. The elders of his community made him see he had no claim.

sources.at: p. 325; the investor and the elders of the community

title: Yusuf and the road costs
body: Yusuf is home from {to}. He says he spent 7 dinars on food, boats and gate fees. He says the house should pay it back. Your orders did not say who pays, and he says a judge would agree with him.

choices.label: Pay him back the 7 dinars
choices.hint: It costs 7 dinars now. Yusuf will trust you.

choices.label: Let a judge decide
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars later. The court thinks well of you. Yusuf does not.

note: One court record shows a quarrel over who paid for the road. The investor said the traveller should. The traveller said the partnership should.

sources.at: pp. 325 to 326; the traveller's costs, and the court record over who pays

title: Hamid never gives accounts
body: Nur is a friend of yours. He has had money with Hamid for years, and Hamid has never given him a full account. Nur asks your house to help. You can ask Hamid for the accounts as partners should, or take him to a judge.

choices.label: Ask him for the accounts
choices.hint: It costs nothing now and brings 5 in two seasons. Hamid may be offended, and Nur will thank you.

choices.label: Take him to a judge
choices.hint: It costs 5 now and pays back 11 in two seasons. The court backs you, but Hamid will be your enemy and partners dislike a house that sues. Nur pays you well.

note: One Geniza partnership went on for ten years before the investor took the manager to court. A usual partnership ran one year at a time, with accounts every year.

sources.at: pp. 326 to 327; the ten years in court, and the yearly accounts

title: A debtor runs to Aydhab
body: A man in Cairo owes your house 12 dinars. He has run off to Aydhab, hoping to escape the debt. Rashid knows where he went.

choices.label: Send a man to find him
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now and pays back 6 in three seasons. The quarrel is in a foreign port, so foreign houses notice.

choices.label: Write to the Beja chief with a gift
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. The chief is pleased, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Give up the debt
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Others hear that your house lets debts go.

note: Aydhab was ruled by the Beja and Egypt together, and Ibn Battuta saw the town split between them in 1326. In older records, a man who owed money might flee there.

title: Posts for the king of Mali
body: The sultan has sent camels and food to help the king of Mali on his pilgrimage. A pilgrimage is a holy journey to Mecca. Zayn, a friend at court, asks you to help feed the animals at the posts on the road.

choices.label: Supply grain for the posts
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The court is glad of your help.

choices.label: Supply it at what it cost you
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. Zayn thanks you, and the court thinks you careful.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Zayn says the court will remember.

note: In 1324 the sultan of Egypt helped Mansa Musa's pilgrimage with silver, camels, food and posts on the road. He wrote to his officers to treat the king with care.

sources.at: p. 78 (al-Umari, Masalik el absar; levtzion-hopkins-1981 pages not reached)

title: Venice may sail again
body: Word comes that the pope has allowed Venice to send some ships to Alexandria again, but only with goods that are allowed. A Venetian trader asks for your help with the sultan's officials.

choices.label: Give a letter of welcome and a warehouse
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. The Venetians favour you for seasons to come.

choices.label: Charge a fee for both
choices.hint: He pays you 4 dinars now. He goes to a rival next time.

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The trader remembers your silence.

note: On 27 April 1344 the pope let Venice send six galleys and six cargo ships to Alexandria for five years. They could carry only allowed goods, and no ship sailed that year.

title: An envoy comes for a treaty
body: A Venetian friend says Venice will send an envoy to the sultan to ask for a new treaty. He asks if you will vouch for his house when the envoy comes.

choices.label: Vouch for his house
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now, for letters. The court thinks well of you, and the envoy may send a thank-you.

choices.label: Lend money to his house
choices.hint: It costs 10 dinars now. The loan helps the Venetians, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The friend is disappointed.

note: In August 1344 Venice decided to send Niccolo Zeno to Egypt as its envoy. He was to ask for a new treaty like the one of 1302.

title: A petition to the king
body: A Florentine trader at Famagusta asks you to join his petition to the king of Cyprus for a lower duty. Florentines pay more than most.

choices.label: Join and pay a share of the gifts
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The rate may fall, and the court thinks well of you.

choices.label: Stand aside
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The Florentines remember who stayed out.

choices.label: Join a rival petition
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. The rival is glad, and partners hear of it.

note: On 21 May 1324 Pegolotti, a Florentine, won a favour from the King of Cyprus. Florentines who paid 4 in 100 would now pay 2, at first for two years.

title: The governor takes the gold
body: A merchant of Tunis died on the road in the west. He left 3,000 gold dinars with a man to take to his heirs. The governor of Bougie has seized the money.

choices.label: Write to the governor's court
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now, a scribe's fee. The court may answer, and it notes your manners.

choices.label: Ask the heirs' friends to press him
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now, a gift to the friends. Foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Accept the loss
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The heirs remember that you did not help.

note: In 1325 a merchant of Tunis died on the road in the west, leaving 3,000 gold dinars for his heirs. The governor of Bougie seized the money, which Ibn Battuta called his first sight of harsh rule.

title: Cloth and tar at his price
body: A court official says he knows you can pay. He offers you cloth, oil and tar at a high price set by the sultan's officials.

choices.label: Buy at his price
choices.hint: It costs 12 dinars now. The official is your friend for seasons to come.

choices.label: Buy half
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. He is a little cold, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Refuse politely
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Your goods may face a slow inspection.

note: From 1333 to 1338 the sultan's officials made merchants buy cloth, wood, furs, iron, cotton, oil and tar at high prices. The practice was stopped in 1341.

title: Envoys from the east
body: Envoys from the broken kingdom of the Mongols have come to Cairo to ask the sultan for friendship. A court friend asks you to help house them.

choices.label: Offer rooms and food
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now. The court is glad of your help.

choices.label: Leave it to the sultan's men
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The friend is a little cold.

choices.label: Send a private gift
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. Foreign houses hear of it, but the sultan's men may frown.

note: In 1336 envoys of the amir Ali Padshah and his khan, Musa, came to the sultan in Cairo. They were well received and given great wealth.
